I don't have any notes for you yet. My first attempt to fetch the sources went wrong, and I ran out of tool calls before I could read any of the pages.

**What happened:** I sent requests for six pages at once: Enduring Word on Isaiah 37, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, Precept Austin, and the NET Bible notes. My code then failed while reading the results, before it had shown me anything from them, and that used up my tool calls for this turn. So I haven't read a single page about Isaiah 37.

Your rules say every point must come from a page I actually read, with its URL, and I mustn't fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I've read nothing, I can't write any verse-by-verse notes now. Anything I wrote would be from memory, and the citations would be unsupported.

**Plan for the next turn:**
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** fetch the six pages above and work through all 38 verses. If the Pulpit or Ellicott page is thin, I'll add StudyLight and Blue Letter Bible.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** search the tradition-specific sites for the verses most likely to divide them. Those are probably Hezekiah's prayer (vv. 14–20), the sign of the three years (v. 30), the remnant (vv. 31–32), "for My servant David" (v. 35), and the angel of the LORD (v. 36). Possible sources include Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, Spurgeon on spurgeon.org, Ligonier, Desiring God, 1517 and Sam Storms.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship (for example, Sennacherib's own account, Tirhakah and the date, and the 185,000), and New Advent, Catholic.com and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings. I'll only cover popular modern teaching such as prosperity or word of faith if the allowed sites actually discuss this chapter.

Reply "continue" and I'll start fetching. Or tell me which verses or traditions matter most and I'll do those first.
